key_insight: At affordable mesh resolution, one parameter set cannot simultaneously match elastic slope, peak force and crack path, so fracture calibration must prioritize a stated objective.
engineering_relevance: Physically consistent fracture calibration can support simulations of brittle-food breakage during production, transport, cutting and mastication.
method: Compare sharp-interface and diffuse phase-field models of Griffith-type brittle fracture in cooled dark chocolate.
Identify elastic parameters from pre-crack tension and compression, then critical energy release rate from three-point-bending peak force.
Calibrate phase-field width last and report the objective, numerical parameters and boundary value problem.
evidence_signal: The case study assesses both frameworks at affordable spatial discretization and finds that phase-field width affects structural response, crack curvature and stress fields.
watch_item: Affordable mesh resolution imposes a lower bound on phase-field width, limiting simultaneous agreement across response metrics.
paper_title: Finite Element Modeling of Fracture in Brittle Foods with Physically Consistent Parameter Calibration: A Practical Case Study on Cooled Dark Chocolate
